title: GRC Management Fundamentals
summary: How organizations govern security, decide on risk and prove what they do: the working model behind every framework, audit and board report, taught without a product in the way.
lede: Governance, risk and compliance are one system with three questions: who decided, what could go wrong, and can we show it. This course teaches that system the way practitioners run it, from the first policy to the board report.
audience: Analysts and engineers moving into GRC, risk or audit roles
Security leaders who own a program but inherited its structure
Founders and operators answering their first customer security review
Consultants and vCISOs who run programs for several organizations
outcomes: Explain how governance, risk and compliance fit together, and what breaks when they don't
Set up the accountability, policy hierarchy and risk appetite a program runs on
Use frameworks and regulations as inputs to one control set, not as separate projects
Run a risk register that ends in recorded, owned decisions
Design controls, test them and keep evidence that stands up in an audit
Run the program on a cadence, with metrics and reporting leadership can act on

lessons.title: What GRC is, and why it exists
lessons.summary: Three questions, one system: what governance, risk and compliance each answer, who does what across the three lines, and why fragmented programs fail.

lessons.title: Governance: direction, accountability and policy
lessons.summary: Charters, committees and decision rights; the policy, standard, procedure and guideline hierarchy; and the risk appetite statement everything else is measured against.

lessons.title: Frameworks, standards and regulations
lessons.summary: What ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, CIS Controls and SOC 2 each are, how laws differ from frameworks, and how one common control set answers many of them.

lessons.title: Risk management: from register to decision
lessons.summary: Identifying and assessing risk, inherent and residual risk, the four treatment options, and why every risk should end in a decision someone owns.

lessons.title: Controls: designing what you rely on
lessons.summary: Control types and categories, writing a control that can be tested, ownership, and keeping a control baseline honest about what is actually implemented.

lessons.title: Assurance: testing, evidence and audits
lessons.summary: Design versus operating effectiveness, what makes evidence audit-ready, how SOC 2 Type I and Type II differ, and handling exceptions and corrective action plans.

lessons.title: Running the program: cadence, metrics and reporting
lessons.summary: The annual, quarterly and monthly rhythm of a GRC program, metrics that drive decisions, and reporting a board can hold the program to.

lessons.title: Beyond the walls: third parties, incidents and change
lessons.summary: Third-party risk across the vendor lifecycle, how incidents feed back into risk and controls, and keeping a program current as the business changes.
